#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install contest AI Coding log collector (official tools: Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex).
# Cursor itself is NOT an official collector target — see notes printed at end.
set -euo pipefail

export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.local/opt/gitroot/usr/bin:$HOME/.local/opt/gitroot/usr/lib/git-core:/usr/bin:$PATH"
export GIT_EXEC_PATH="${GIT_EXEC_PATH:-$HOME/.local/opt/gitroot/usr/lib/git-core}"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$HOME/.local/opt/gitroot/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

CONTEST="${HOME}/openvela/contest2026_004_TeamFalcons"
INSTALLER="${HOME}/openvela/.claude/skills/contest-log-collector/onboarding/install.sh"

TEAM_ID="${TEAM_ID:-contest2026_004_TeamFalcons}"
GITHUB_LOGIN="${GITHUB_LOGIN:-FoLeaf}"

if [[ ! -d "$CONTEST" ]]; then
  echo "Contest repo missing. Finish repo sync first."
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -f "$INSTALLER" ]]; then
  echo "Log collector not present at $INSTALLER"
  echo "It should appear after repo sync (openvela/.claude)."
  exit 1
fi

cd "$CONTEST"
bash "$INSTALLER" --team-id "$TEAM_ID" --github-login "$GITHUB_LOGIN"

VERIFY="${HOME}/openvela/.claude/skills/contest-log-collector/onboarding/verify-setup.sh"
if [[ -f "$VERIFY" ]]; then
  bash "$VERIFY" || true
fi

mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
grep -q 'HOME/.local/bin' ~/.bashrc || echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc

cat <<'NOTE'

==== 重要：Cursor 与日志归集 ====
大赛官方自动采集仅支持：Claude Code / AIoT-IDE / OpenCode / Codex。
Cursor 对话目前无法计入有效工时。

推荐工作流（适配 Cursor 编译调试 + 合规日志）：
1. 日常写代码 / Build / Download / F5：Cursor Remote-WSL（本仓已配置）
2. 需要计入工时的 AI 会话：在 ~/openvela 内另开 Claude Code 或 Codex CLI
3. 会话结束后检查 logs/<github_login>/ 并 git add logs/

若 GITHUB_LOGIN 不是你本人，请编辑 ~/.claude/contest-collector.env

90	def load_redact_rules(log_root: Path) -> list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]]:
91	    custom_path = log_root / "redact.json"
92	    if not custom_path.exists():
93	        return DEFAULT_REDACT_RULES
94	    try:
95	        custom = json.loads(custom_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
96	        compiled = []
97	        for r in custom:
98	            flags = 0
99	            if "i" in r.get("flags", ""):
100	                flags |= re.IGNORECASE
101	            compiled.append((re.compile(r["pattern"], flags), r.get("replacement", "***REDACTED***")))
102	        return [*DEFAULT_REDACT_RULES, *compiled]
103	    except Exception:
104	        return DEFAULT_REDACT_RULES

107	def redact_value(value: Any, rules: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]], counter: list[int]) -> Any:
108	    if isinstance(value, str):
109	        out = value
110	        for pattern, replacement in rules:
111	            new_out, n = pattern.subn(replacement, out)
112	            counter[0] += n
113	            out = new_out
114	        return out
115	    if isinstance(value, list):
116	        return [redact_value(v, rules, counter) for v in value]
117	    if isinstance(value, dict):
118	        return {k: redact_value(v, rules, counter) for k, v in value.items()}
119	    return value

140	def expand_claude_event(raw_event: dict, fallback_ts: str) -> list[dict]:
141	    """Convert one Claude Code transcript event to zero-or-more contest events.
142	
143	    Schema (verified against real ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl):
144	      - top-level type: user / assistant / system / progress / file-history-snapshot / ...
145	      - real conversation lives in .message
146	      - assistant.message.content is a list of blocks: text / thinking / tool_use
147	      - user.message.content is str (plain input) OR list (containing tool_result blocks)
148	      - tool_result blocks carry tool_use_id pairing back to assistant tool_use
149	    """
150	    out: list[dict] = []
151	    top_type = raw_event.get("type")
152	    ts = raw_event.get("timestamp") or fallback_ts
153	
154	    if top_type in ("progress", "file-history-snapshot", "queue-operation", "permission-mode", "agent-name", "summary", "attachment"):
155	        return out
156	
157	    msg = raw_event.get("message") or {}
158	    role = (msg.get("role") or top_type or "system").lower()
159	    content = msg.get("content")
160	    model = msg.get("model")
161	    usage = msg.get("usage") or {}
162	    tokens_in = usage.get("input_tokens")
163	    tokens_out = usage.get("output_tokens")
164	
165	    common = {"ts": ts}
166	    if model:
167	        common["model"] = model
168	    if isinstance(tokens_in, int):
169	        common["tokens_in"] = tokens_in
170	    if isinstance(tokens_out, int):
171	        common["tokens_out"] = tokens_out
172	
173	    if isinstance(content, str):
174	        if content:
175	            out.append({**common, "role": role, "text": content})
176	        return out
177	
178	    if not isinstance(content, list):
179	        return out
180	
181	    for block in content:
182	        if not isinstance(block, dict):
183	            continue
184	        bt = block.get("type")
185	        if bt in SKIP_BLOCK_TYPES:
186	            continue
187	        if bt == "text":
188	            text = block.get("text", "")
189	            if text:
190	                out.append({**common, "role": role, "text": text})
191	        elif bt == "thinking":
192	            thinking = block.get("thinking") or block.get("text") or ""
193	            if thinking:
194	                out.append({**common, "role": role, "thinking": thinking})
195	        elif bt == "tool_use":
196	            out.append({
197	                **common,
198	                "role": "tool",
199	                "tool_name": block.get("name", "unknown"),
200	                "tool_call_id": block.get("id", f"call_{len(out)}"),
201	                "input": block.get("input"),
202	                "output": None,
203	            })
204	        elif bt == "tool_result":
205	            tool_call_id = block.get("tool_use_id", f"call_{len(out)}")
206	            result_content = block.get("content")
207	            out.append({
208	                **common,
209	                "role": "tool",
210	                "tool_name": "<result>",
211	                "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
212	                "input": None,
213	                "output": result_content,
214	                "is_error": bool(block.get("is_error")),
215	            })
216	        else:
217	            out.append({
218	                **common,
219	                "role": role,
220	                "text": f"[unsupported block type: {bt}]",
221	                "metadata": {"dropped": True, "original_type": bt},
222	            })
223	    return out

240	def parse_cursor_embedded_timestamp(text: str) -> str | None:
241	    """Parse `<timestamp>Monday, Aug 17, 2026, 5:00 PM (UTC+8)</timestamp>`."""
242	    if not text:
243	        return None
244	    match = _CURSOR_TS_RE.search(text)
245	    if not match:
246	        return None
247	    raw = " ".join(match.group(1).split())
248	    tz_match = _CURSOR_TZ_RE.search(raw)
249	    offset = timezone.utc
250	    if tz_match:
251	        sign = 1 if tz_match.group(1) == "+" else -1
252	        hours = int(tz_match.group(2))
253	        minutes = int(tz_match.group(3) or 0)
254	        offset = timezone(sign * timedelta(hours=hours, minutes=minutes))
255	        raw = raw[: tz_match.start()].strip()
256	    for fmt in ("%A, %b %d, %Y, %I:%M:%S %p", "%A, %b %d, %Y, %I:%M %p"):
257	        try:
258	            dt = datetime.strptime(raw, fmt).replace(tzinfo=offset)
259	            utc = dt.astimezone(timezone.utc)
260	            return utc.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.") + f"{utc.microsecond // 1000:03d}Z"
261	        except ValueError:
262	            continue
263	    return None

266	def expand_cursor_event(raw_event: dict, fallback_ts: str, raw_index: int = 0,
267	                        default_model: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:
268	    """Convert one Cursor agent-transcript JSONL line to contest events.
269	
270	    Schema (verified against ~/.cursor/projects/*/agent-transcripts/*/*.jsonl):
271	      - top-level role: user / assistant (often NOT copied into message.role)
272	      - no top-level type on conversation lines; type=turn_ended is a marker
273	      - message.content is a list of text / thinking / tool_use blocks
274	      - tool_use blocks frequently omit id
275	      - user text may wrap <timestamp> ... <user_query>
276	    """
277	    top_type = (raw_event.get("type") or "").lower()
278	    if top_type in CURSOR_SKIP_TYPES:
279	        return []
280	
281	    msg = raw_event.get("message") or {}
282	    role = (msg.get("role") or raw_event.get("role") or top_type or "").lower()
283	    if not role or role in CURSOR_SKIP_TYPES:
284	        return []
285	    if role not in ("user", "assistant", "system", "tool"):
286	        return []
287	
288	    text_for_ts = ""
289	    content = msg.get("content")
290	    if isinstance(content, str):
291	        text_for_ts = content
292	    elif isinstance(content, list):
293	        text_for_ts = _extract_text_content(content)
294	    ts = (
295	        raw_event.get("timestamp")
296	        or parse_cursor_embedded_timestamp(text_for_ts)
297	        or fallback_ts
298	    )
299	    model = msg.get("model") or raw_event.get("model") or default_model
300	    usage = msg.get("usage") or {}
301	    tokens_in = usage.get("input_tokens")
302	    tokens_out = usage.get("output_tokens")
303	
304	    common: dict[str, Any] = {"ts": ts}
305	    if model:
306	        common["model"] = model
307	    if isinstance(tokens_in, int):
308	        common["tokens_in"] = tokens_in
309	    if isinstance(tokens_out, int):
310	        common["tokens_out"] = tokens_out
311	
312	    if isinstance(content, str):
313	        if content:
314	            return [{**common, "role": role, "text": content}]
315	        return []
316	
317	    if not isinstance(content, list):
318	        return []
319	
320	    out: list[dict] = []
321	    for block_i, block in enumerate(content):
322	        if not isinstance(block, dict):
323	            continue
324	        bt = block.get("type")
325	        if bt in SKIP_BLOCK_TYPES:
326	            continue
327	        if bt == "text":
328	            text = block.get("text", "")
329	            if text:
330	                out.append({**common, "role": role, "text": text})
331	        elif bt == "thinking":
332	            thinking = block.get("thinking") or block.get("text") or ""
333	            if thinking:
334	                out.append({**common, "role": "assistant" if role == "assistant" else role,
335	                            "thinking": thinking})
336	        elif bt == "tool_use":
337	            tool_call_id = (
338	                block.get("id")
339	                or block.get("tool_use_id")
340	                or f"cursor_{raw_index}_{block_i}"
341	            )
342	            out.append({
343	                **common,
344	                "role": "tool",
345	                "tool_name": block.get("name", "unknown"),
346	                "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
347	                "input": block.get("input"),
348	                "output": None,
349	            })
350	        elif bt == "tool_result":
351	            out.append({
352	                **common,
353	                "role": "tool",
354	                "tool_name": "<result>",
355	                "tool_call_id": block.get("tool_use_id") or f"cursor_{raw_index}_{block_i}",
356	                "input": None,
357	                "output": block.get("content"),
358	                "is_error": bool(block.get("is_error")),
359	            })
360	        elif bt:
361	            out.append({
362	                **common,
363	                "role": role,
364	                "text": f"[unsupported block type: {bt}]",
365	                "metadata": {"dropped": True, "original_type": bt},
366	            })
367	    return out

370	def find_cursor_transcript(session_id: str, cwd: str | None = None,
371	                           transcript_path: str | None = None) -> Path | None:
372	    """Locate ~/.cursor/projects/*/agent-transcripts/<sid>/<sid>.jsonl."""
373	    if transcript_path:
374	        path = Path(transcript_path)
375	        if path.is_file():
376	            return path
377	    if not session_id:
378	        return None
379	    projects = Path.home() / ".cursor" / "projects"
380	    if not projects.is_dir():
381	        return None
382	    matches: list[Path] = []
383	    try:
384	        for jsonl in projects.glob(f"*/agent-transcripts/{session_id}/*.jsonl"):
385	            if jsonl.is_file():
386	                matches.append(jsonl)
387	        for jsonl in projects.glob(f"*/agent-transcripts/{session_id}.jsonl"):
388	            if jsonl.is_file():
389	                matches.append(jsonl)
390	    except Exception:
391	        return None
392	    if not matches:
393	        return None
394	    if cwd:
395	        hint = Path(cwd).name.lower()
396	        hinted = [m for m in matches if hint and hint.lower() in str(m).lower()]
397	        if len(hinted) == 1:
398	            return hinted[0]
399	        if hinted:
400	            return max(hinted, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)
401	    return max(matches, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)

404	def _extract_text_content(content: Any) -> str:
405	    parts: list[str] = []
406	    if isinstance(content, str):
407	        return content
408	    if not isinstance(content, list):
409	        return ""
410	    for block in content:
411	        if isinstance(block, dict) and block.get("type") == "text":
412	            parts.append(str(block.get("text", "")))
413	        elif isinstance(block, str):
414	            parts.append(block)
415	    return "\n".join(p for p in parts if p)

418	def append_events(jsonl_path: Path, events: list[dict], session_id: str, team_id: str, github_login: str, tool: str, start_seq: int, redact_rules) -> dict:
419	    seq = start_seq
420	    redacted_total = 0
421	    lines = []
422	    for ev in events:
423	        counter = [0]
424	        redacted = redact_value(ev, redact_rules, counter)
425	        redacted_total += counter[0]
426	        out = {
427	            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
428	            "session_id": session_id,
429	            "team_id": team_id,
430	            "github_login": github_login,
431	            "tool": tool,
432	            "seq": seq,
433	            **redacted,
434	        }
435	        if counter[0] > 0:
436	            out["redacted_count"] = counter[0]
437	        lines.append(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False))
438	        seq += 1
439	    if not lines:
440	        return {"written": 0, "last_seq": start_seq - 1, "redacted": 0}
441	    jsonl_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
442	    with jsonl_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
443	        f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
444	    return {"written": len(lines), "last_seq": seq - 1, "redacted": redacted_total}

451	def read_manifest(member_dir: Path, team_id: str, github_login: str, tool: str) -> dict:
452	    path = member_dir / "manifest.json"
453	    if not path.exists():
454	        return {
455	            "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
456	            "team_id": team_id,
457	            "github_login": github_login,
458	            "generator": f"{tool}-collector@{VERSION}",
459	            "updated_at": iso_now(),
460	            "sessions": [],
461	        }
462	    try:
463	        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
464	        if not raw.strip():
465	            raise json.JSONDecodeError("Expecting value", raw, 0)
466	        data = json.loads(raw)
467	        if data.get("team_id") != team_id:
468	            report_error(member_dir, "manifest_team_mismatch", {"tool": tool, "path": str(path)},
469	                         f"manifest.team_id={data.get('team_id')} but TEAM_ID env={team_id}")
470	        if data.get("github_login") and data.get("github_login") != github_login:
471	            report_error(member_dir, "manifest_login_mismatch", {"tool": tool, "path": str(path)},
472	                         f"manifest.github_login={data.get('github_login')} but detected={github_login}")
473	        return data
474	    except Exception as e:
475	        report_error(member_dir, "manifest_read", {"tool": tool, "path": str(path)}, e)
476	        # Never fall back to sessions=[] when a file already exists — that wipe
477	        # path previously destroyed the full contest index after a concurrent
478	        # non-atomic write left an empty/truncated manifest.
479	        raise ManifestCorruptError(f"corrupt manifest at {path}: {e}") from e

3	description: Use when configuring ZCode's extension resources (MCP servers, slash commands, skills, hooks, and plugins) or instruction files such as AGENTS.md in the ZCode client. Explains where each resource is configured at the user and workspace scope, the discovery order, precedence, and merge rules, plus guidance on which location to choose. 4	---
5	
6	# ZCode Configuration Guide
7	
8	ZCode supports five types of extension resources, plus AGENTS.md instruction files. This skill is the **map**: it tells you where each resource is configured and how conflicts are resolved. For "something is not working, how do I fix it," follow the routing to the `diagnosing-*` skills at the end.
9	
10	## How things are configured
11	
12	There are two ways to work with configuration in the ZCode client, and this plugin serves both:
13	
14	- **A person** manages resources through the client's graphical interface — **Settings → Plugin Management**, **Settings → Skills**, **Settings → Subagents**, **Settings → MCP**, and the **`/` menu** in the input box.
15	- **An agent** repairs configuration by reading and editing the underlying files directly with its file tools. The locations and rules below are what an agent uses to find the right file and field.
16	
17	## Scopes and the main configuration files
18	
19	- **User scope** — lives under your home directory and applies to every workspace.
20	- **Workspace scope** — lives inside a repository and applies only to that project; can be shared with a team through version control.
21	- **User configuration file**: `~/.zcode/cli/config.json`. Holds MCP servers, hooks, plugin enable/disable state, and skill/command disable overrides.
22	- **Workspace configuration file**: `<repo>/.zcode/config.json` (or `<repo>/zcode.json`).
23	- **User instruction file**: `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`. Applies as default instructions for every workspace.
24	- **Workspace instruction file**: `<repo>/AGENTS.md`. Applies only to that project; the current workspace path is searched upward until the project root.
25	
26	## The five resources at a glance
27	
28	| Resource | Form | User scope | Workspace scope | Conflict rule |
29	|---|---|---|---|---|
30	| **Skills** | Directory + `SKILL.md` | `~/.zcode/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/` | `<repo>/.zcode/skills/`, `<repo>/.agents/skills/` | Identity is the file path; on load the **first same-named skill wins** (user scope has priority) |
31	| **Commands** | `.md` file | `~/.zcode/commands/`, `~/.agents/commands/` | `<repo>/.zcode/commands/`, `<repo>/.agents/commands/` | Deduplicated by normalized command name; **first match wins** (user scope overrides workspace), the loser is ignored |
32	| **MCP** | JSON object | `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` → `mcp.servers` (fallback `~/.agents/mcp.json` → `mcpServers`) | `<repo>/.zcode/config.json` → `mcp.servers` (fallback `<repo>/.agents/mcp.json` → `mcpServers`) | **User overrides workspace** for a same-named server; workspace-scoped servers are **trusted and auto-connected** by default, same as user-scoped |
33	| **Hooks** | `hooks.json` / config object | `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` → `hooks` | `<repo>/.zcode/config.json` → `hooks` | Configuration-file hooks require `hooks.enabled: true`; plugin hooks are appended |
34	| **Plugins** | Directory + `plugin.json` | Installed from a marketplace; enable/disable state stored in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` | — | A plugin contributes skills, commands, hooks, MCP servers, and agents |
35	| **Instructions** | `AGENTS.md` file | `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md` | `<repo>/AGENTS.md` | User default instructions load first, then workspace instructions load later so the workspace can narrow or override broad defaults |
36	
37	> Note: `.agents/mcp.json` is a **compatibility fallback** for MCP. Within each scope the client reads `.zcode` first; only if that scope has no MCP servers does it fall back to `.agents/mcp.json` (which uses a top-level `mcpServers` key, whereas `.zcode` uses nested `mcp.servers`).
38	
39	## Instructions / AGENTS.md: merge order
40	
41	`AGENTS.md` is not a skill, command, hook, MCP server, or plugin. It is the instruction file ZCode loads into the model context for broad behavior rules.
42	
43	- **User scope**: `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`. Use this for personal defaults that should apply in every workspace, such as preferred language, review style, or local workflow conventions.
44	- **Workspace scope**: `<repo>/AGENTS.md`. Use this for repository-specific rules that should be shared with the project, such as architecture boundaries, logging rules, testing requirements, and commit/MR policy.
45	- **Resolution**: ZCode searches for the workspace `AGENTS.md` from the current working directory upward until the detected project root. The user default file is resolved from the user's home directory.
46	- **Merge order**: when both files exist, ZCode injects `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md` first, then the resolved workspace `AGENTS.md`. Workspace instructions appear later, so they can narrow or override broad user defaults for that repository.
47	- **Migration and creation**: onboarding can copy Claude user memory from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`. The built-in `/init` command targets the current workspace `AGENTS.md`, creating or updating repository instructions instead of editing the user default file.
48	
49	## Skills and commands: discovery order (identical)
50	
51	Locations are scanned in this order (earlier locations take precedence):
52	
53	1. Explicitly configured roots
54	2. User `~/.zcode/skills` (or `commands`)
55	3. User `~/.agents/skills`
56	4. Workspace `.zcode/skills` (from the current directory up to the repository root; every level counts)
57	5. Workspace `.agents/skills`
58	6. Enabled **plugin** roots (lowest precedence)
59	
60	Within a level, `.zcode` is scanned before `.agents`. A deeper working-directory location takes precedence over a repository-root location.
61	
62	- **Skills merge**: identity is the file path, so same-named skills at different paths are **all discovered**, but only the first in discovery order is loaded — higher-precedence copies shadow the rest.
63	- **Commands merge**: the key is the normalized command name, and the **first match wins**; duplicates are ignored. Nested directories join into the name with a colon: `review/code.md` becomes `/review:code` (not `/review/code`).
64	
65	## MCP: merge and auto-connect
66	
67	- **Override order** for a same-named server: CLI override → environment → user → workspace → system defaults. In short, **user overrides workspace**. Plugin-provided servers form the base layer and are overridden by explicit configuration.
68	- **Auto-connect**: MCP servers from every scope — user, **workspace**, plugin, environment, and CLI — are **trusted and connected automatically** at session start. (Workspace-scoped servers were previously untrusted and required manual authorization; they now connect by default like any other scope.) Use **Settings → MCP** to inspect status and repair server configuration.
69	
70	## Hooks: essentials
71	
72	- Supported events (exactly seven): `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`.
73	- **Configuration-file hooks must set `hooks.enabled: true`** to run (disabled by default). When any plugin contributes a hook, the hook runner is enabled automatically.
74	
75	## Plugins: essentials
76	
77	- Managed in **Settings → Plugin Management** (the **Installed** and **Discover** tabs). A plugin directory carries a manifest at `.zcode-plugin/plugin.json` (the compatibility names `.claude-plugin/` and `.codex-plugin/` are also recognized). The minimal manifest requires only `name` (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`).
78	- Component fields: `commands`, `skills`, `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `agents` (each may be a directory name, an array, or inline). The fields `channels`, `lspServers`, `outputStyles`, and `settings` are recorded but not executed.
79	- Enable/disable state is stored under `plugins` in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json`. A built-in plugin can be disabled but not uninstalled.
80	- Marketplaces can be added (via the **`+`** button on the Discover tab) from a GitHub repository, a Git URL, a local directory, or a file.
81	
82	## Choosing where to configure
83	
84	- Personal, used across projects → user scope (`~/.zcode/...` or `~/.agents/...`).
85	- Team- or project-shared, versioned with the repository → workspace scope (`<repo>/.zcode/...` or `.agents/...`).
86	- Shared across tools (Claude, Codex, Cursor) → put skills in `~/.agents/skills/`; to override a same-named skill only inside ZCode, use `.zcode/skills/`.
87	- Personal default instructions → `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`; repository-specific instructions → `<repo>/AGENTS.md`. If both exist, keep broad preferences in the user file and project rules in the workspace file.
88	- MCP servers → user configuration for personal servers, or workspace configuration to share with a team; both scopes connect automatically. Because opening a project now auto-connects the MCP servers declared in its configuration, only open workspaces you trust.
89	- Secrets → never commit them to version control; use environment variables or local settings.
90	
91	## When something is wrong — route to a diagnostic skill
92	
93	When a configuration is read but has no effect, or reports an error, load the matching skill. Each provides a symptom → cause → check → fix workflow, covering both what to click in the client and which file and field an agent should edit:
94	
95	- MCP server not connecting, tools missing, untrusted, or timing out → **`diagnosing-mcp`**
96	- A skill is not discovered, not triggering, shadowed, or disabled → **`diagnosing-skills`**
97	- A `/command` is missing, overridden, has a frontmatter error, or arguments do not substitute → **`diagnosing-commands`**
98	- A hook does not trigger, its matcher does not match, its script is not executable, or it blocks unexpectedly → **`diagnosing-hooks`**
99	- A plugin is not listed, fails to install, has missing components, or is not enabled → **`diagnosing-plugins`**

4	---
5	
6	# Diagnosing Hook Configuration
7	
8	Goal: reduce any hook problem to a single concrete fix.
9	
10	> Note on trust: plugin hooks execute regardless of the marketplace they came from — third-party plugin hooks run just like built-in ones. Any "diagnostic-only until trusted" wording you may see for marketplace hooks is stale; a plugin's detail view marks each hook as runnable, and that is now true for all hooks.
11	
12	## 1. Configuration sources and merging
13	
14	- **Configuration-file hooks**: the top-level `hooks` key in `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` (or the workspace `<repo>/.zcode/config.json` / `zcode.json`), shaped as `{ enabled?, timeoutMs?, maxOutputBytes?, events: { <Event>: [ { matcher?, hooks: [...] } ] } }`. **These are disabled by default — configuration-file hooks must set `hooks.enabled: true` to run.**
15	- **Plugin hooks**: each plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` (or its manifest `hooks` field). Plugin matchers are appended after configuration matchers. **When any plugin contributes a hook, the hook runner is enabled automatically.**
16	- Non-plugin (user or workspace) configuration hooks have no trust gate; with `enabled: true` they run unconditionally.
17	
18	## 2. hooks.json schema
19	
20	```json
21	{ "hooks": { "<Event>": [ { "matcher": "...", "hooks": [ { "type": "command"|"process", ... } ] } ] } }
22	```
23	
24	(A plugin file uses the outer `hooks` wrapper; the configuration file uses `hooks.events.<Event>`. The inner array is the same.)
25	
26	- **Event names (exactly seven)**: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`. Any other name is an unsupported event. (Events such as `Notification`, `SubagentStop`, and `PreCompact` are **not** supported.)
27	- **The matcher is a case-sensitive regular expression**, tested against the event's match value:
28	  - `SessionStart` → one of `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`
29	  - Tool events (`PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUseFailure`) → the **tool name** (`Bash`, `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Agent`, …), with aliases `Task` ↔ `Agent` and `Write`/`Edit` ← `ApplyPatch`
30	  - `UserPromptSubmit` → the prompt text; `Stop` → the response preview
31	  - An omitted matcher matches everything; an invalid regular expression never matches (silently)
32	- **`type: "command"`**: `command` (a shell string); optional `shell`, `timeout` (in **seconds**), `timeoutMs` (in milliseconds, takes precedence), and `statusMessage`. Note that `async` currently has no runtime effect.
33	- **`type: "process"`**: `command` (an executable) plus `args[]` (an argument vector run without a shell, the most portable choice), `timeoutMs` (in **milliseconds**), and `statusMessage`.
34	- Timeout resolution: `timeoutMs` → `timeout × 1000` → the configuration's `timeoutMs` → a default of 60000 ms.
35	- Template variables (expanded in the command and each argument, and also injected as environment variables): `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` / `${ZCODE_PROJECT_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}`; and, for plugin hooks only, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` / `${ZCODE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and the plugin data directory. Note that a skill-directory variable is not valid in a hook and raises an error.
36	- **Hook output**: standard output is parsed as JSON (a strict schema — any extra key fails validation), or you may use exit codes: `0` passes, `2` blocks (a deny for `PreToolUse`/`PermissionRequest`), and any other non-zero raises an error. `additionalContext` is injected into the conversation; `PreToolUse` may return a permission decision of `allow`/`ask`/`deny`; `Stop` may request continuation (up to three times).
37	
38	## 3. How to inspect hooks
39	
40	- **In the client**: **Settings → Plugin Management** → open a plugin's detail view to see the hooks it registers and whether each is runnable.
41	- **As an agent**: read the `hooks/hooks.json` (or the manifest `hooks` field) for a plugin, and the `hooks` block of `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` / the workspace config for configuration hooks.
42	- **Execution** (fired, timed out, blocked) is recorded in the ZCode log, with the hook's source, matcher, outcome, duration, and a preview of its error stream — enough to distinguish a timeout from a failure from a block.
43	
44	## 4. Common pitfalls (symptom → cause → fix)
45	
46	1. **Configuration-file hooks do not run** — you added `hooks.events.*` but nothing fires. They are disabled by default and are enabled automatically only when a plugin hook is present. → Set `"hooks": { "enabled": true, ... }` in the configuration.
47	2. **Wrong event name** — the hook never triggers. → Use exactly one of the seven supported events.
48	3. **Matcher does not match (tool name, case, or regex)** — it is registered but never fires for the tool you expect. The matcher is a case-sensitive regular expression; `"bash"` will not match `Bash`, and an invalid expression never matches. → Use the exact tool name or a correct expression (for example `"Edit|Write"`), or omit the matcher to match all. Remember the aliases `Task` → `Agent` and `Write`/`Edit` → `ApplyPatch`.
49	4. **Script is not executable** — `permission denied`, with a failed outcome. The script was installed without the executable bit. → Run `chmod +x` on it, or invoke it through an interpreter, e.g. `{"type":"command","command":"bash \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh\""}`, so the executable bit is irrelevant.
50	5. **Template variable not expanded** — a literal `${...}` or an empty path. Only recognized variables are expanded; a skill-directory variable raises an error inside a hook, and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is available only for plugin hooks. → Use only supported variables, and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` for plugin-relative paths.
51	6. **Timeout unit mistaken** — the hook is killed with a timed-out outcome. `command`'s `timeout` is in **seconds**; `process`'s `timeoutMs` is in **milliseconds**. `timeout: 500` means 500 seconds; `timeoutMs: 5` means 5 milliseconds. → Use `"timeout": <seconds>` for a command hook and `"timeoutMs": <milliseconds>` for a process hook.
52	7. **Command and process fields mixed** — the hook is dropped. A `process` hook accepts only `command`, `args`, and `timeoutMs`; a `command` hook accepts `command`, `shell`, `timeout`, and `timeoutMs`. → Match the fields to the `type`.
53	8. **JSON output fails validation** — the hook ran but its effect was discarded and the run marked failed. The output was not valid JSON, contained an extra key (the schema is strict), or its event-specific output named the wrong event. → Emit only the recognized keys with the correct event name, or emit nothing (empty output is fine) and rely on exit codes.
54	9. **Assuming `async` runs in the background** — you set `async: true` but the session still waits. The `async` field has no runtime effect and hooks always run inline. → Do not rely on `async`; for background work, have the script daemonize itself.
55	10. **Cross-platform failure** — it works on one operating system but not another. A `command` hook runs through a shell, so POSIX syntax fails on Windows. → Prefer a `process` hook (an argument vector, no shell), or ship a polyglot wrapper script and keep hook scripts extensionless.
56	11. **A hook blocks the session unexpectedly** — a tool is denied or the run halts. The hook returned a block, exited with code 2, or returned a `deny` decision. → Inspect the block's reason in the log; fix the script's exit code — return 0 to pass and reserve 2 for a deliberate block.
57	12. **Believing third-party hooks are "diagnostic only"** — a third-party plugin hook did not run and you suspect a trust gate. That is not the cause: all plugin hooks are runnable. → Diagnose via pitfalls 2, 3, 4, and 8.
58	
59	## 5. Localization workflow (in order)
60	
61	1. **Is a runner active?** Confirm that either `hooks.enabled: true` is set in the configuration or at least one plugin contributes a hook; otherwise no runner exists and every hook is skipped.
62	2. **Enumerate what is registered.** In **Settings → Plugin Management**, open the plugin's detail view and confirm the hook you expect is present and runnable, and that its plugin is enabled. For configuration hooks, read the `hooks` block directly.
63	3. **Event name and matcher.** Check against the seven events; confirm the match value and the case-sensitive expression; test by omitting the matcher (which matches everything).
64	4. **Executable and interpreter.** Confirm the script has its executable bit, or invoke it explicitly via `bash`/`node`.
65	5. **Run it by hand.** Feed a sample hook input to the script and inspect the exit code and output — `0` plus valid JSON is healthy, `2` is a deliberate block, any other non-zero is a failure.
66	6. **Observe live.** Trigger the event and read the hook run records in the log (outcome, duration, error-stream preview) to distinguish a timeout from a failure from a block.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Export AI Coding sessions from staging into the demo repo's logs/ directory.
4	
5	Staging path:  ~/.claude/contest-collector-staging/<github_login>/<date>/<tool>__<sid>.jsonl
6	Target path:   <repo_root>/logs/<github_login>/<date>/<tool>__<sid>.jsonl
7	
8	Normally sessions auto-export into the demo repo's logs/ at session end
9	(see the adapters). This script is the manual path: list, re-export, or
10	selectively export staged sessions.
11	
12	Usage:
13	  python3 tools/export-session.py --latest
14	  python3 tools/export-session.py --session <session-id>
15	  python3 tools/export-session.py --since <date>
16	  python3 tools/export-session.py --all
17	  python3 tools/export-session.py --list
18	"""
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import argparse
22	import json
23	import shutil
24	import sqlite3
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
28	from pathlib import Path
29	
30	
31	def staging_root() -> Path:
32	    return Path.home() / ".claude" / "contest-collector-staging"
33	
34	
35	def _load_env_github_login() -> str | None:
36	    env_file = Path.home() / ".claude" / "contest-collector.env"
37	    if not env_file.is_file():
38	        return None
39	    try:
40	        for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
41	            if line.startswith("GITHUB_LOGIN="):
42	                val = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
43	                return val or None
44	    except Exception:
45	        return None
46	    return None
47	
48	
49	def repo_root() -> Path | None:
50	    try:
51	        out = subprocess.check_output(
52	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
53	            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
54	        )
55	        return Path(out.strip())
56	    except Exception:
57	        return None

60	def list_sessions(github_login: str | None) -> list[dict]:
61	    root = staging_root()
62	    if not root.exists():
63	        return []
64	    if github_login is None:
65	        env_login = _load_env_github_login()
66	        if env_login:
67	            github_login = env_login
68	    sessions = []
69	    for member_dir in sorted(root.iterdir()):
70	        if not member_dir.is_dir() or member_dir.name == "errors":
71	            continue
72	        if github_login and member_dir.name != github_login:
73	            continue
74	        manifest_path = member_dir / "manifest.json"
75	        if not manifest_path.exists():
76	            continue
77	        try:
78	            manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
79	        except Exception:
80	            continue
81	        for s in manifest.get("sessions", []):
82	            sessions.append({
83	                "github_login": member_dir.name,
84	                "session_id": s.get("session_id"),
85	                "tool": s.get("tool"),
86	                "started_at": s.get("started_at", ""),
87	                "last_event_at": s.get("last_event_at", ""),
88	                "event_count": s.get("event_count", 0),
89	                "file_path": s.get("file_path", ""),
90	                "model": s.get("model", ""),
91	            })
92	    return sessions
93	
94	
95	def filter_sessions(sessions: list[dict], args) -> list[dict]:
96	    if args.session:
97	        return [s for s in sessions if s["session_id"] == args.session]
98	    if args.latest:
99	        if not sessions:
100	            return []
101	        return [max(sessions, key=lambda s: s.get("last_event_at") or "")]
102	    if args.since:
103	        try:
104	            cutoff = datetime.fromisoformat(args.since.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
105	        except ValueError:
106	            cutoff = datetime.combine(
107	                datetime.strptime(args.since, "%Y-%m-%d").date(),
108	                datetime.min.time(), tzinfo=timezone.utc,
109	            )
110	        if cutoff.tzinfo is None:
111	            cutoff = cutoff.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
112	        result = []
113	        for s in sessions:
114	            ts = s.get("last_event_at") or s.get("started_at") or ""
115	            try:
116	                ev_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
117	                if ev_dt.tzinfo is None:
118	                    ev_dt = ev_dt.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
119	                if ev_dt >= cutoff:
120	                    result.append(s)
121	            except ValueError:
122	                continue
123	        return result
124	    if args.today:
125	        today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()
126	        result = []
127	        for s in sessions:
128	            ts = s.get("last_event_at") or s.get("started_at") or ""
129	            try:
130	                ev_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(ts.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
131	                if ev_dt.date() == today:
132	                    result.append(s)
133	            except ValueError:
134	                continue
135	        return result
136	    if args.all:
137	        return sessions
138	    return []

141	def copy_session(s: dict, dest_repo: Path, dry_run: bool) -> tuple[bool, str]:
142	    src_root = staging_root() / s["github_login"]
143	    src_jsonl = src_root / s["file_path"].split(f"{s['github_login']}/", 1)[-1] \
144	        if "logs/" in s["file_path"] else None
145	    if src_jsonl is None or not src_jsonl.exists():
146	        date_part, fname = None, None
147	        if s["file_path"].count("/") >= 2:
148	            parts = s["file_path"].split("/")
149	            date_part, fname = parts[-2], parts[-1]
150	        if date_part and fname:
151	            src_jsonl = src_root / date_part / fname
152	    if not src_jsonl or not src_jsonl.exists():
153	        return False, f"source jsonl not found for session {s['session_id']}"
154	
155	    rel_inside = src_jsonl.relative_to(src_root)
156	    dest_jsonl = dest_repo / "logs" / s["github_login"] / rel_inside
157	
158	    if dry_run:
159	        return True, f"[dry-run] would copy {src_jsonl} -> {dest_jsonl}"
160	
161	    dest_jsonl.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
162	    shutil.copy2(src_jsonl, dest_jsonl)
163	
164	    actual_count = sum(1 for line in dest_jsonl.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip())
165	    s["event_count"] = actual_count
166	    s["file_path"] = f"logs/{s['github_login']}/{rel_inside}"
167	
168	    update_dest_manifest(s, dest_repo)
169	    return True, f"copied -> {dest_jsonl.relative_to(dest_repo)} ({actual_count} events)"

172	def update_dest_manifest(s: dict, dest_repo: Path) -> None:
173	    member_dir = dest_repo / "logs" / s["github_login"]
174	    manifest_path = member_dir / "manifest.json"
175	    if manifest_path.exists():
176	        manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
177	    else:
178	        src_manifest_path = staging_root() / s["github_login"] / "manifest.json"
179	        src_manifest = json.loads(src_manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
180	        manifest = {
181	            "schema_version": src_manifest.get("schema_version", "1.0"),
182	            "team_id": src_manifest.get("team_id", ""),
183	            "github_login": s["github_login"],
184	            "generator": src_manifest.get("generator", ""),
185	            "sessions": [],
186	        }
187	    existing = next((x for x in manifest["sessions"]
188	                     if x.get("session_id") == s["session_id"]), None)
189	    src_manifest_path = staging_root() / s["github_login"] / "manifest.json"
190	    src_manifest = json.loads(src_manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
191	    src_entry = next((x for x in src_manifest.get("sessions", [])
192	                      if x.get("session_id") == s["session_id"]), None)
193	    if src_entry is None:
194	        return
195	    entry = dict(src_entry)
196	    if "event_count" in s:
197	        entry["event_count"] = s["event_count"]
198	    if "file_path" in s:
199	        entry["file_path"] = s["file_path"]
200	    if existing:
201	        existing.update(entry)
202	    else:
203	        manifest["sessions"].append(entry)
204	    manifest["updated_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
205	    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
206	                             encoding="utf-8")

def expand_zcode_message(message: dict, parts: list[dict], fallback_ts: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Convert one ZCode db message (+ its parts) to contest events.

    Schema (verified against ~/.zcode/cli/db/db.sqlite):
      - message.data: role, time.created (ms), modelID, tokens.{input,output}
      - part.data types: text / reasoning / tool / step-start / step-finish / timeline
      - tool parts merge input and output into one block (state.input / state.output)
    """
    data = message  # dict
    role = str(data.get("role") or "").lower()
    if role not in ("user", "assistant", "system", "tool"):
        return []
    time_info = data.get("time") or {}
    created_ms = time_info.get("created")
    ts = _millis_to_iso(created_ms) if created_ms else fallback_ts

    common = {"ts": ts}
    model = data.get("modelID")
    tokens = data.get("tokens") or {}
    if model:
        common["model"] = model
    if isinstance(tokens.get("input"), int):
        common["tokens_in"] = tokens["input"]
    if isinstance(tokens.get("output"), int):
        common["tokens_out"] = tokens["output"]

    out = []
    for part in parts:
        ptype = part.get("type")
        if ptype in ZCODE_SKIP_PART_TYPES or ptype is None:
            # timeline parts carry no type, only timelineType
            if not (ptype is None and part.get("timelineType")):
                if ptype is not None:
                    continue
            continue
        if ptype == "text":
            text = part.get("text") or ""
            if text:
                out.append({**common, "role": role, "text": text})
        elif ptype == "reasoning":
            thinking = part.get("text") or ""
            if thinking:
                out.append({**common, "role": role, "thinking": thinking})
        elif ptype == "tool":
            state = part.get("state") or {}
            out.append({

                "role": "tool",
                "tool_name": part.get("tool") or "unknown",
                "tool_call_id": part.get("callID") or f"zcode_{len(out)}",

    return out

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ZCODE_REDACT_RULES = [
    (re.compile(r"sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"), "sk-***REDACTED***"),
    (re.compile(r"ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}"), "ghp_***REDACTED***"),
    (re.compile(r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-+/=]+"), "Bearer ***REDACTED***"),
]


def _redact(value):
    if isinstance(value, str):
        out = value
        for pattern, replacement in ZCODE_REDACT_RULES:
            out = pattern.sub(replacement, out)
        return out
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_redact(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _redact(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    return value
